evidence.quote:
his wet feet numb and stinging with cold inside his torn
overshoes which could not be replaced until next winter, and then only
if the Karadi did not decrease the clothing ration still further.
evidence.paraphrase: An alien authority called the Karadi controls rationing of basic goods like clothing.

evidence.quote: the scars and stumps of buildings that remained of what had been the city.
evidence.paraphrase: The city is left in ruins, a changed world.

evidence.quote:
the gas range which had been
converted to wood when the Karadi suspended all public utilities
evidence.paraphrase: The Karadi have suspended public utilities, forcing a regression in daily life.

evidence.quote:
The Karadi had outlawed all
wonder drugs, all hospitals, all medical schools. Helpless, they had
watched George die
evidence.paraphrase: Medicine has been outlawed, leading to preventable deaths such as their son George's.
Listening to short-wave radio carries a death penalty under the regime.

evidence.quote:
since the day the Karadi came
swooping down from space and
caught the world in a tired breathing spell in World War III.
evidence.paraphrase: The Karadi are alien invaders who arrived from space during World War III, twenty years earlier.

evidence.quote:
Freddie was flying a Karadi plane against the last strongholds of free
man in the Rocky Mountains.
evidence.paraphrase: Conscripted humans pilot advanced Karadi aircraft against remaining free humans.

evidence.quote:
They don't need us, our resources. They feed on what we feel.
They are a--a sadistic fungi.
evidence.paraphrase: A character theorizes the aliens sustain themselves on human emotional suffering rather than material resources.

evidence.quote:
although with their invincible weapons they had
disarmed all the world's armies and, instead of rebuilding, had made a
shambles of our civilization.
evidence.paraphrase: The aliens used superior weapons to disarm all human militaries and dismantle civilization.

evidence.quote:
It took me two years to build that short-wave out of spare
parts, but it was worth every minute.
evidence.paraphrase: Mr. Davidson constructed a short-wave radio from spare parts to gather information.

evidence.quote:
Freddie is dead. Because they tell us, that's no reason to believe.
How can we believe? We saw Freddie alive, but now they tell us Freddie
is dead.
evidence.paraphrase: Mrs. Friedlander struggles to accept her son's reported death because she has no proof.

evidence.quote:
Mr. Friedlander felt a spring in his step he hadn't felt for twenty
years
evidence.paraphrase: Mr. Friedlander feels renewed hope upon learning his son may be alive.

evidence.quote:
Only it was like the cat he once had read about.
You took the cat and gave it food, catnip, but every time it ate you
also fed it electricity, a shock.
evidence.paraphrase: He compares the Karadi's cultivation of doubt to a conditioning experiment that torments a subject amid abundance.

evidence.quote:
He walked up the six snow-covered
steps to the police station, went inside, sat down and started telling
the uniformed figure at the desk about the subversives in his building
who owned short-wave radios
evidence.paraphrase: Overwhelmed by doubt and self-interest, Mr. Friedlander informs on his neighbors to the authorities.

evidence.quote:
The new generation hardly remembered the
delightful old foods, but if Mr. Friedlander shut his eyes and thought,
he could clearly smell steak and roast chicken and broiled lobster
swimming in butter
evidence.paraphrase: The present impoverished diet is contrasted with remembered pre-invasion abundance.
